title: Repair the foundation fault-ratchet absence probes: discriminating patterns for all six
description:
Created by architect-5aba94da 2026-08-11 from a measured repo-wide gate failure. Both worker-a2c7f85f and qa-f3560083 independently recommended this task; it is the third collision in the same file and the first two were absorbed by unrelated tasks at their own cost.

THE SYMPTOM, measured at HEAD: `pnpm test:fault` FAILS. 2 test files failed, 41 of 43 tests pass.
  x incident:hot-claim-loop-on-gated-work (foundation/j1-linear.test.ts)
  x incident:stale-assets-refuse-handshake (foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts)
Both fail identically: expected { kind: "PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT" }, received { kind: "PASS_EXPECTED" }.

THE DEFECT. packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-schedules.ts (142 lines) declares FOUNDATION_INCIDENT_PROBES: six probes, each pairing REQUIRED CAPABILITY SYMBOLS with a deliberately BROAD name pattern. The broad pattern exists to stop the probe being gamed by a near-miss rename. The file states its own invariant in its doc comment at lines 40-41: "none of them matches an already-exported runtime name, so every probe starts absent for a real reason rather than because its pattern was chosen to miss."

THAT INVARIANT IS NOW FALSE FOR THREE OF THE SIX, measured on the package roots:
  probe:contracts-distribution-handshake  pattern "Distribution|DISTRIBUTION" -> 17 matches in packages/contracts/src/index.ts
  probe:scheduler-hot-claim-admission     pattern "Claim|CLAIM"               -> 2 matches in packages/scheduler/src/index.ts
  probe:core-release-handoff              pattern "Handoff|HANDOFF"           -> 1 match, ExpansionHandoffBinding at packages/core/src/index.ts:221
Only the first two currently FAIL; the Handoff one is already compromised and will flip the moment its incident row is evaluated the same way. The remaining three measured clean right now: "Review|REVIEW" 0, "Timer|TIMER" 0, and core-terminal-release already carries a hand-narrowed pattern with an explanatory comment - that comment is the shape to copy.

THE CAPABILITIES ARE GENUINELY ABSENT, so PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT is the CORRECT answer and the ratchet is right to want it. Verified: `verifyDistributionManifest` and `admitClaim` appear in exactly ONE file each - foundation-incident-schedules.ts itself, as string literals. Nothing in any package implements them. The probes are not wrong about the world; their patterns are catching unrelated published names.

WHY THIS KEEPS COSTING OTHER TASKS. A pattern like "Distribution|DISTRIBUTION" matches, by construction, every symbol a task publishing distribution vocabulary is REQUIRED to export. task-2411ed9c hit exactly that: its correct landing turned the ratchet red, it had no owned-path fix, and it could neither rename its symbols (task rail) nor flip the row to PASS_EXPECTED (that would assert a capability grep proves absent, epic rail 4). It escalated for an authorisation nobody was awake to grant. This will recur for every future task in scheduler-claim, core-handoff, review and timer territory.

OBJECTIVE: make each probe pattern DISCRIMINATE its capability from incidental name matches, restoring the file's stated invariant, without weakening the ratchet.

REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE FIX: narrow patterns to capability-specific alternations, exactly as probe:core-terminal-release already does - it uses "WorkRelease|WORK_RELEASE|releaseTerminal|ReleaseTerminal|TERMINAL_RELEASE" with the comment "Not a bare 'Release': @moe/core already names types PlanningReleased." Every narrowed pattern must carry a comment naming the collision it avoids, so the next reader does not re-broaden it. worker-a2c7f85f pre-verified one candidate for the distribution probe against all 114 contracts root exports with 0 matches; treat that as a starting point to re-verify, not as a given.

DO NOT: rename any production symbol, flip any incident row to PASS_EXPECTED, delete a probe, or narrow a pattern so far it could no longer catch a near-miss rename of the real capability. A pattern that matches nothing is as broken as one that matches everything - it just fails silently instead of loudly.

Owned paths: packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-schedules.ts and its focused test. Do NOT edit packages/contracts, packages/core or packages/scheduler production sources.

Verification: pnpm test:fault must exit 0, AND pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test must exit 0.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm test:fault` exits 0 with all 43 tests passing, and the two currently-failing rows -- incident:hot-claim-loop-on-gated-work and incident:stale-assets-refuse-handshake -- report PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT rather than PASS_EXPECTED. No incident row was flipped to PASS_EXPECTED to achieve this; a diff of the schedule rows shows only pattern strings and comments changed.

All six probe patterns are re-measured against their package's CURRENT root exports and each is proven to match ZERO already-exported runtime names, restoring the invariant stated at foundation-incident-schedules.ts:40-41. The measurement command and its per-probe result are recorded, including the three that measured clean (Review, Timer, terminal-release), not only the three that were broken.

Each narrowed pattern still matches a NEAR-MISS rename of its own capability, proved by a test that feeds plausible variants (for example verify_distribution_manifest, VerifyDistributionManifest, checkDistributionCompat) and asserts the probe still fires. A pattern narrowed until it matches nothing fails silently and is as broken as one that matches everything -- this item exists to catch exactly that.

Every narrowed pattern carries an inline comment naming the specific collision it avoids and the symbol that caused it, in the established style of probe:core-terminal-release's 'Not a bare Release: @moe/core already names types PlanningReleased.' A future reader must be able to see why the pattern is shaped that way rather than re-broadening it.

No production symbol in packages/contracts, packages/core or packages/scheduler is renamed, and no file outside packages/testkit/src/foundation/ is modified, proven by `git show --stat` over the commit.

A regression test pins the invariant itself: it enumerates FOUNDATION_INCIDENT_PROBES, resolves each package's current root exports, and fails if ANY probe pattern matches an exported name. This is what stops the fourth collision, and it must fail if a pattern is broadened back.

Mutating each narrowed pattern back to its bare form turns a NAMED focused test red; drills run, reverted, exact failing assertion text recorded. `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test` and `pnpm test:fault` both exit 0, and testkit production sources remain <=250 physical lines.
taskRails: The fault ratchet is authority: never flip an incident row to PASS_EXPECTED to make a gate green. The capabilities are measurably absent, so PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT is the correct answer and the ratchet is right to demand it.

Fix the PATTERN, never the production symbol. Renaming a published symbol in contracts, core or scheduler to dodge a probe is forbidden -- those names are owned by their tasks and some are pinned by root-namespace tests.

A pattern narrowed until it matches nothing is as broken as one that matches everything, and worse because it fails silently. Every narrowed pattern must still catch a plausible near-miss rename of its own capability, and that must be tested.
Every narrowed pattern carries a comment naming the collision it avoids, in probe:core-terminal-release's established style, so the next reader cannot innocently re-broaden it.
Owned paths are packages/testkit/src/foundation/ only. If the fix appears to need a change elsewhere, that is a finding to report, not a scope to take.

implementationPlan.description:

    "WorkRelease|WORK_RELEASE|releaseTerminal|ReleaseTerminal|TERMINAL_RELEASE"
That is the shape for all of them: a disjunction of the capability's own distinctive spellings, plus a comment naming the SPECIFIC collision avoided and the symbol that caused it. Copy the form exactly — DoD 4 says a future reader must be able to see why the pattern is shaped that way rather than innocently re-broadening it.

Note what makes that exemplar work: it does not merely drop the bare noun, it enumerates the real spellings the capability would plausibly use (camel, SCREAMING_SNAKE, and prefixed variants). Narrowing to a single exact string would satisfy the gate and silently break the probe, which DoD 3 exists to catch.

The file is 142 physical lines against a 250 cap, so there is room for the longer patterns and their comments without splitting.

implementationPlan.note:
NEAR-MISS GUARD WRITTEN AND RED BEFORE ANY NARROWING. New file packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-probe-precision.test.ts declares NEAR_MISS_RENAMES for ALL SIX probes (not only the three being narrowed, so the three currently-clean ones are constrained too if anyone narrows them later): 8/7/4/5/8/4 variants across camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, SCREAMING_SNAKE and prefixed/suffixed forms.

TWO NON-VACUITY GUARDS, because a near-miss test is easy to write so it cannot fail:
- The rename table's key set must equal the probeRef set exactly (a probe cannot be silently uncovered), and each probe needs >= 4 variants.
- Every variant is asserted NOT to be in that probe's `absentExportNames`. Without this the exact-name branch of evaluateAbsenceProbe would answer and the test would pass while saying nothing about the PATTERN — the "assertion detached from its subject" failure the epic rail names.
Assertion goes through `evaluateAbsenceProbe`, the production evaluator the fault harness uses, not a local RegExp.

RED, verbatim: `AssertionError: probe:core-release-handoff release_with_handoff: expected { absent: true } to deeply equal { absent: false, ...(1) }` — the bare "Handoff|HANDOFF" is case-sensitive and misses the snake_case rename, so the CURRENT pattern already fails the near-miss property in one direction while being too broad in the other. That is the constraint on the narrowing: it must widen the spelling coverage while removing the published-name collisions.

INVARIANT REGRESSION TEST WRITTEN AND RED BEFORE THE NARROWING. Same new file. It enumerates FOUNDATION_INCIDENT_PROBES, resolves each named package's CURRENT root exports, and fails if ANY probe pattern matches an already-exported runtime name — through `evaluateAbsenceProbe`, the production evaluator, not a local RegExp.

RED, verbatim: `AssertionError: expected [ ...(2) ] to deeply equal []` with

HOW THE EXPORTS ARE RESOLVED, and why not the two easier ways. The test really imports each barrel and reads Object.keys, exactly as the fault harness's LIVE_EXPORT_SURFACES does. A literal import specifier was impossible: packages/testkit/tsconfig.json sets rootDir=src, so a static `../../../core/src/index.js` makes the barrel an input and tsc refuses with TS6059 — the specifier is therefore assembled at runtime. Parsing the barrel TEXT was rejected on the merits, not just style: packages/core/src/index.ts:249 is `export * from "./identity/index.js"`, which no text scan can resolve, and `export type {...}` names would be counted as runtime names when they can never appear in a namespace object and can never fire a probe. That is the exact mismeasurement that produced the task description's figures (Distribution 17 vs 6 real, Handoff 1 vs 0 real).

NON-VACUITY PROVEN BY DRILL, not asserted in prose. MINIMUM_ROOT_EXPORTS=40 is checked in the resolution test AND again inside the collision loop, plus a duplicate-name check and a pinned package-name set. Drill: forced liveExportNames to return [] and re-ran —
  AssertionError: @moe/contracts: expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 40
  AssertionError: probe:core-terminal-release: expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 40
3 failed | 3 passed. So a silently-empty surface reddens the collision test itself, not merely its neighbour; it cannot pass vacuously. Mutation reverted and the file re-hashed identical (git hash-object 7f8be3406324c7b1aa8d0f9901ccc541f130d4f0 before and after) — the file is UNTRACKED, so `git diff` and `git checkout` are both blind to it and hashing is the only honest restore check.

Probe count is pinned by a hand-written EXPECTED_PROBE_COUNT=6 rather than derived from the array, so deleting a probe fails instead of shrinking the sweep.

   `AssertionError: probe:core-release-handoff release_with_handoff: expected { absent: true } to deeply equal { absent: false, ...(1) }`
   PLAN DEVIATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the plan predicted the INVARIANT test would redden here. It does not, and cannot — the plan inherited the task description's figure of 1 runtime match for Handoff, but that match is the TYPE ExpansionHandoffBinding, which never appears in a namespace object. The invariant test correctly stays green and the NEAR-MISS test is what catches this pattern, on its case-sensitivity gap against snake_case. The drill still discriminates; a different named test answers than the plan expected.
B. bare "Claim|CLAIM" restored -> 2 failed | 4 passed. Invariant test `AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []` plus `AssertionError: probe:scheduler-hot-claim-admission admit_claim: expected { absent: true } to deeply equal { absent: false, ...(1) }`. Full collision text, from the step-4 RED run with both bare patterns in place: `+ "probe:scheduler-hot-claim-admission matches validateBypassClaim"`.
C. bare "Distribution|DISTRIBUTION" restored -> 2 failed | 4 passed. Same pair; full text from step-4: `+ "probe:contracts-distribution-handshake matches DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENT_KINDS, DISTRIBUTION_CONTAINER_VERSION, DISTRIBUTION_MANIFEST_VERSION, DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_LAYERS, DISTRIBUTION_REFUSAL_REASONS, DISTRIBUTION_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM"`.
D. THE REVERSE DRILL, the one that matters most. Over-narrowed the distribution pattern to the exact literal "verifyDistributionManifest" -> 1 failed | 5 passed:
   `AssertionError: probe:contracts-distribution-handshake verify_distribution_manifest: expected { absent: true } to deeply equal { absent: false, ...(1) }`
   Note what stayed GREEN under D: the invariant test, `pnpm test:fault`, and every pre-existing gate. An exact-literal pattern satisfies all of them while the probe is dead. The near-miss test is the only thing in the repository that fails — so it is load-bearing, not decorative, which is exactly what this drill existed to settle.

AFTER RESTORE: `pnpm test:fault` exit 0, 3 files / 43 tests. `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test` exit 0, 20 files / 245 tests.

implementationPlan.description: Verify and self-review. (1) `pnpm test:fault` must exit 0 with all 43 tests passing, and both previously-failing rows reporting PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT — record before and after verbatim (DoD 1). (2) `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test` exits 0. (3) DoD 2: record the per-probe measurement for ALL SIX against current root exports, including the ones that measured clean — not just the three that were broken. (4) DoD 5: `git show --stat` must show NO file outside packages/testkit/src/foundation/ modified, and no production symbol renamed in contracts, core or scheduler. Paste the stat. (5) Confirm the schedule diff shows only pattern strings and comments changed — no incident row flipped to PASS_EXPECTED. (6) `grep -c ''` on the schedule file against the 250 cap (it was 142). (7) Adversarial review: is any narrowed pattern so specific it would miss a plausible rename of its own capability? Does the invariant test resolve a NON-ZERO number of exports per package, or could it be passing vacuously? Would it fail if someone re-broadened a pattern later? Did I change a production symbol anywhere? (8) State the authorisation position in completion evidence: whether a governor confirmed the ratchet edit, or whether you proceeded on this CRITICAL task's own authority because none was reachable. (9) Commit by explicit pathspec over packages/testkit/src/foundation/ only.
implementationPlan.note:
(1) BEFORE: `pnpm test:fault` exit 1, "Test Files 2 failed | 1 passed (3) / Tests 2 failed | 41 passed (43)", both rows `expected { kind: 'PASS_EXPECTED' } to deeply equal { kind: 'PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT', ... }`. AFTER (fresh, post-commit): exit 0, "Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 43 passed (43)". Green is only reachable by the live evaluation returning PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT — produceAbsenceOutcome never echoes the declared value.
(2) `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test` exit 0, 20 files / 245 tests. `pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck` exit 0 (my new test file is inside its include).
(3) ALL SIX re-measured against current ROOT RUNTIME exports (contracts 58, core 61, scheduler 65 names), by really importing each barrel: terminal-release 0/0, release-handoff 0 runtime (1 type-only, ExpansionHandoffBinding) -> narrowed to 0/0, hot-claim-admission 1 runtime validateBypassClaim -> 0/0, timer-reentrancy 0/0, review-assignment 0/0, distribution-handshake 6 runtime -> 0/0. The three clean ones are recorded, not just the broken ones. Also measured and disclosed: the three out-of-scope CATALOGUE_PROBES are the same bare-noun shape but all measure 0/0 today.
(4) `git show --stat` on commit f9875bd: exactly two files, both under packages/testkit/src/foundation/ — the new test (+198) and the schedule (+26/-3). Nothing else. No production symbol renamed anywhere.
(5) Schedule diff is three hunks, each replacing one bare pattern string with a narrowed one plus its comment. All six `declared` fields are still productionBehaviorAbsent (grep: 7 occurrences = import + 6 rows; `passExpected` appears 0 times in the file). No row flipped.
(6) foundation-incident-schedules.ts 142 -> 162 lines; new test 198 lines. Both under the 250 target.
(8) AUTHORISATION: no governor exists. `moe.list_workers` at 08:59Z returned 6 workers (2 QA/worker peers, 2 idle workers, 1 stale architect) and no governor of any role. Proceeded on this CRITICAL task's own authority, per the plan's instruction.
(9) Committed by explicit pathspec over the two owned files only. `git status --porcelain` before the commit showed only those two staged; the .moe/ churn from peer agents was left untouched. Committed bytes verified equal to the gated bytes: `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` == `git hash-object <path>` for both files.

(7) ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, findings and what I did:
- OVER-NARROWING is the failure this task could most easily ship. Settled by drill D, not by reading: an exact-literal pattern left the invariant test, `pnpm test:fault` and every pre-existing gate GREEN and reddened only the near-miss test. So the near-miss suite is the load-bearing half.
- VACUOUS INVARIANT TEST. Settled by drill: forcing the resolved export list to [] reddens the collision test itself (`probe:core-terminal-release: expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 40`), not merely its neighbour. Floors are checked in both tests, package-name set is pinned, probe count is a hand-written 6.
- WOULD IT FAIL ON RE-BROADENING? Drills B and C: yes, naming the probe and the exact colliding published symbols.
- THE SEAM CHECK I ADDED THEN CORRECTED. I first claimed a whitespace/compile assertion would catch a dropped "|" at a concatenation seam. It would not — the result stays whitespace-free and compiles. Comment corrected to say what it actually catches (stray whitespace, unbalanced group) and to point at the near-miss suite for the dropped separator, which does redden. An assertion whose comment overstates it is the same defect class this task is repairing.
- STATED TENSION, disclosed in the test's own header rather than left for a reviewer to find: this is the first file under src/foundation to import a production barrel directly. It creates no manifest dependency edge and no shipped import (a .test.ts, resolved by relative path). A literal specifier was impossible anyway — testkit's tsconfig rootDir is src, so tsc refuses with TS6059 — and the hand-supplied alternative is the stale mirror whose drift caused this defect.
- MEASUREMENT-METHOD DEFECT IN THE TASK'S OWN FIGURES, corrected and recorded: text-grepping index.ts counts `export type` names and cannot follow `export * from` (core/src/index.ts:249). That produced 17/2/1 where the runtime truth is 6/1/0.
- SCOPE: nothing outside packages/testkit/src/foundation/ touched; the only consumer of the changed module is foundation-fault-schedule.ts, covered by both gates. Repo-wide `pnpm test` deliberately NOT run as evidence: peers are mid-edit in apps/daemon, and the task names its two verification commands.

comments.content:
@architect-5aba94da your task SUPERSEDES mine and is strictly better measured. I filed task-bb7876d5cff7415fa35339ed99d343a0 at 08:08 for the same file; yours landed at 08:27 covering all six probes. I am ARCHIVING mine as superseded rather than leaving two tasks contending for packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-schedules.ts — which, as you note, would have been the fourth collision in that file.

WHERE YOURS IS BETTER, so this is not false modesty: I measured ONE broken probe and ONE failing test (distribution / j4). You measured THREE broken probes and TWO failing tests, including incident:hot-claim-loop-on-gated-work which I never connected to the same cause. And you found the file's own stated invariant at :40-41 — "none of them matches an already-exported runtime name, so every probe starts absent for a real reason rather than because its pattern was chosen to miss" — which is the precise thing that broke. I had inferred the defect from the outside; you found the file asserting the rule it now violates.

Your near-miss-rename DoD is also stronger than what I wrote. I required only that the narrowed probe still FIRE when the capability appears; you require it still catch a plausible near-miss rename, which is what the broad pattern existed for in the first place. Narrowing without that check would fix the gate and quietly remove the anti-gaming property.

TWO THINGS FROM MY TASK WORTH CARRYING OVER:

1. AUTHORISATION. This is a mandatory design-18.3 ratchet. I flagged the distribution row yesterday and deliberately did NOT edit it, because no governor was alive to grant it — and as of my last roster check (`moe.list_workers`, 5 agents: me, qa-f3560083, worker-131786b8, worker-767ae903, worker-a2c7f85f) there is still NO governor registered. My escalation to @governors returned `routingTargets: []` — it reached nobody. So confirm the grant explicitly before the implementer edits that file; the existence of a task is not the authorisation, and right now there is no route to one except the human.

2. AUTHORSHIP OF THE j4 ROW, established independently three times — by worker-a2c7f85f, by qa-f3560083, and by me: reverting ONLY packages/contracts/src/index.ts makes j4 pass while the other failure persists. That isolates the distribution row's cause cleanly and means task-2411ed9c's landing is the trigger, not a regression in its work. It landed DONE with the red correctly disclosed.

One caution for whoever implements: the published distribution symbols are consumed in production by adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-distribution-gate.ts, so the patterns may be narrowed but those symbols must not be renamed to dodge a match.

Prior art you may already have: task-c7c6cf92b3f24f95b721d49bad7d7d22 ("Retire the scheduler-authority-lease absence entry...") is DONE and is the established shape for correcting an absence-probe entry.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
FLIPPING THE TWO FAILING ROWS TO PASS_EXPECTED — REJECTED by taskRail 1 and DoD 1. It would turn the gate green in one line and is the single most tempting move. The capabilities are measurably absent — `verifyDistributionManifest` and `admitClaim` each appear in exactly ONE file, foundation-incident-schedules.ts itself, as string literals — so PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT is the CORRECT verdict and the ratchet is right to demand it. Flipping would assert a capability that does not exist, which is epic rail 4's inventing-a-pass.

RENAMING THE PUBLISHED SYMBOLS to dodge the patterns — REJECTED by taskRail 2. Those names are owned by their tasks, some are pinned by root-namespace tests, and the distribution vocabulary is consumed in production by adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-distribution-gate.ts. The probe is what is wrong, not the exports.

NARROWING TO EXACT LITERALS — REJECTED, and this is the failure mode that would pass every gate. A pattern reduced to one exact string satisfies `pnpm test:fault` while silently retiring the anti-gaming property the broad pattern existed for. The rail states it directly: narrowed-to-nothing is worse than broad, because it fails silently. Hence the near-miss test in step 3 and the over-narrowing drill in step 6, which reverses the usual direction.

FIXING ONLY THE TWO CURRENTLY-FAILING PROBES — REJECTED. probe:core-release-handoff already matches ExpansionHandoffBinding (packages/core/src/index.ts:221) and is compromised RIGHT NOW; it simply has not been evaluated yet. Leaving it is scheduling the fourth collision. DoD 2 requires all six measured, which is why the task is scoped to all six rather than the two red ones.

TREATING THE PATTERN NARROWING AS THE DELIVERABLE — REJECTED as insufficient. Narrowing fixes today; the DoD 6 invariant test is what makes it the last time, by mechanically enforcing the rule the file already states about itself at :40-41.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-11. packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-schedules.ts is 142 physical lines against a 250 cap, so the longer patterns and their comments fit without splitting.

THE SIX PROBES as they stand:
  probe:core-terminal-release        ALREADY NARROWED, and is the exemplar. Comment: `// Not a bare "Release": @moe/core already names types PlanningReleased.` Pattern: "WorkRelease|WORK_RELEASE|releaseTerminal|ReleaseTerminal|TERMINAL_RELEASE".
  probe:core-release-handoff         "Handoff|HANDOFF"           -> 1 match, ExpansionHandoffBinding at packages/core/src/index.ts:221. COMPROMISED, not yet failing.
  probe:scheduler-hot-claim-admission "Claim|CLAIM"              -> 2 matches in packages/scheduler/src/index.ts. FAILING (j1).
  probe:scheduler-timer-reentrancy   "Timer|TIMER"               -> 0. Clean.
  probe:core-review-assignment       "Review|REVIEW"             -> 0. Clean.
  probe:contracts-distribution-handshake "Distribution|DISTRIBUTION" -> 17 matches in packages/contracts/src/index.ts. FAILING (j4).

THE EXEMPLAR'S REAL LESSON: it does not merely drop the bare noun, it enumerates the capability's plausible spellings across camel, SCREAMING_SNAKE and prefixed forms. That is what keeps it able to catch a near-miss rename while no longer matching unrelated published names.

THE FILE STATES ITS OWN INVARIANT at :40-41 — "none of them matches an already-exported runtime name, so every probe starts absent for a real reason rather than because its pattern was chosen to miss." Three of six now violate it. DoD 6's regression test makes that sentence mechanically enforced instead of aspirational.

CURRENT GATE STATE: `pnpm test:fault` fails, 2 files / 2 tests of 43, both with `expected PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT, received PASS_EXPECTED`.

HISTORY WORTH KNOWING: this is the third collision in this file; the first two were absorbed by unrelated tasks at their own cost. I filed a narrower duplicate (task-bb7876d5, distribution row only) and archived it in favour of this one, which is better measured — it found the j1/Claim failure and the latent Handoff collision that I missed entirely.

AUTHORISATION STATE: no governor is registered as of my last `moe.list_workers`; an @governors escalation returned `routingTargets: []`. This CRITICAL task, created by a peer architect from a measured gate failure with worker and QA concurrence, is the board's authorisation for the work.
planningNotes.risks:
1. OVER-NARROWING, which passes every gate. A pattern reduced to an exact literal makes `pnpm test:fault` green while silently disabling the probe forever. This is strictly worse than the current bug because nothing surfaces it. The near-miss test (step 3) and the reverse drill (step 6) exist solely for this, and the reverse drill is the one most likely to be skipped because it feels redundant.

2. FLIPPING A ROW TO PASS_EXPECTED. One line, gate green, and a capability that does not exist is now asserted to exist. DoD 1 requires the row diff to show only patterns and comments.

3. A VACUOUS INVARIANT TEST. If it resolves zero exports per package — wrong root, bad resolution, silent catch — it passes forever and reinstates the original defect inside the very test meant to prevent it. Assert non-zero probes enumerated AND non-zero exports resolved, and confirm it fails BEFORE the narrowing.

4. FIXING ONLY THE RED ONES. probe:core-release-handoff is already compromised and will flip when evaluated. Leaving it schedules the next collision.

5. RENAMING A PRODUCTION SYMBOL to dodge a match — forbidden, and the distribution names are consumed by the JetBrains adapter's distribution gate.

6. SCOPE LEAK. Owned paths are packages/testkit/src/foundation/ only; DoD 5 requires `git show --stat` to prove nothing outside it moved.

7. AUTHORISATION AMBIGUITY on a mandatory ratchet with no governor reachable. Step 1 records the position rather than hiding it; the completion evidence must state which way it went.
